text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's Austrian newspapers:

- Metal industry becomes first sector to adopt flexible working hours for its 90,000 employees. Workers can work between 32 to 45 hours per week and get time compensation of 15 minutes for every hour of overtime.
- Erste chief Konrad Fuchs retires early and Andreas Treichl is tipped to take over the top job at the savings bank.
- Special session of parliament to discuss the issue of unemployment today. Freedom Party head Joerg Haider has said he wants out-of-work foreigners to be sent back to their home country.
- National grid company Verbund is gearing itself up financially in preparation of the coming liberalisation of the electricity market.
- Do-it-yourself chain bauMax plans to invest one billion schillings this year and to expand into Italy and Croatia.
- Austria's postal system is unimpressed by the WTO agreement as "a lowering of rates was already on our agenda."
- Die Erste forecasts that the ATX index will have climbed to around 1,340 points within the next 12 months due to relatively cheap valuations. The ATX is presently trading around 1,200.
- Lauda Air is in cooperation talks with Malaysian Airlines and a deal could be signed by autumn.

- The Austrian National Bank's stash of gold is not only being eyed by Freedom Party head Haider. Even Social Democrat circles are now thinking about whether it would be possible to use part of the huge reserves for the budget.

- CA Leasing chalked up substantial profit gain in 1996. Pretax profit jumped to 137.1 million schillings after 43.3 million in 1995. The company expects further profit growth due to the merger of its parent company Creditanstalt-Bankverein with Bank Austria.
- Foreign Minister and People's Party chief Wolfgang Schuessel said "a new NATO is also an option for us."
